questions.stem: The reward for the entrepreneur as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: Profit is what remains after land, labour and capital have been paid, which is why it can be negative. That residual character is precisely what makes the entrepreneur the risk bearer.

distractorRationale.a: Rent is the reward to land
distractorRationale.b: Interest is the reward to capital
distractorRationale.d: A salary is a form of wage and is the reward to labour, including a hired manager

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of land as a factor of production?

options.text: It is man-made and depreciates with use
It is fixed in total supply and geographically immobile
It cannot be separated from its owner
It is always homogeneous in quality

questions.explanation: Land is a free gift of nature whose total quantity cannot be increased, and a hectare in Sokoto cannot be carried to Lagos. These two features explain why rent rises so sharply where land is in demand.

distractorRationale.a: Being man-made and depreciating describes capital
distractorRationale.c: Inseparability from the owner describes labour
distractorRationale.d: Land is markedly heterogeneous: fertility, minerals and location differ from place to place

questions.stem: In economics, capital is best described as

options.text: the money held in a firm's bank account
man-made assets used to produce further goods and services
the total value of a firm's annual sales
all the free gifts of nature used in production

questions.explanation: Capital means produced means of production — machines, buildings, tools and stocks of materials. Money is only a claim on resources; it becomes capital when it is used to acquire such assets.

distractorRationale.a: Money in the bank is a financial claim, not itself a productive asset
distractorRationale.c: Annual sales are revenue, a flow measured over time
distractorRationale.d: Free gifts of nature are land

questions.stem: The most important limitation on the extent to which division of labour can be applied is

options.text: the rate of interest on loans

questions.explanation: Splitting a process into many specialised tasks only pays if output is large enough to keep each specialist busy. A tailor selling ten shirts a week cannot employ separate cutters, sewers and finishers, however skilled they are.

distractorRationale.b: Worker age affects individual productivity, not whether tasks can be subdivided
distractorRationale.c: Interest rates affect the cost of capital rather than the scope for specialisation
distractorRationale.d: Taxation affects profitability but not the technical possibility of dividing tasks

questions.stem: A disadvantage of the division of labour is that

options.text: it reduces the total output of the firm
it increases the time spent moving between tasks
it makes work monotonous and leaves workers occupationally immobile
it prevents the use of machinery in production

questions.explanation: Repeating one narrow task destroys variety and the satisfaction of completing a whole article, and a worker skilled only in that task struggles to move to another industry if the firm closes. Both costs fall on the worker rather than the firm.

distractorRationale.a: Division of labour raises total output; that is its main purpose
distractorRationale.b: It saves such time, because workers stay at one operation
distractorRationale.d: It actively encourages the use of machinery by making each task repetitive and standardised

questions.stem: Labour is described as a perishable factor of production because

options.text: an hour of labour not used today cannot be stored and used tomorrow
wages must be paid in cash at the end of each month
workers can move from one occupation to another

questions.explanation: Unlike a machine or a bag of cement, labour services cannot be warehoused. A worker idle today has lost that day's productive capacity permanently, which is why unemployment is such a costly waste for an economy.

distractorRationale.a: Retirement concerns the length of working life, not the storability of labour services
distractorRationale.c: The method of paying wages is an accounting matter
distractorRationale.d: Movement between occupations describes occupational mobility, a different characteristic

questions.stem: The efficiency of labour depends only on the natural ability of the worker.
questions.explanation: False. Output per worker also depends on education and training, health and nutrition, the level of wages, the quality of capital equipment, the standard of management and the conditions of work. This is why the same worker is more productive in a better-equipped firm.

distractorRationale.a: This ignores every factor a firm or a country can actually change, and would make investment in training pointless

questions.stem: A tailoring business earns ₦6,000,000 in revenue. It pays shop rent of ₦600,000, interest of ₦300,000, wages of ₦2,880,000 and material costs of ₦1,500,000. What is the profit accruing to the entrepreneur, in naira? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Total costs are ₦600,000 + ₦300,000 + ₦2,880,000 + ₦1,500,000 = ₦5,280,000. Profit is the residual: ₦6,000,000 − ₦5,280,000 = ₦720,000. Because profit is what is left over, it would have been negative had revenue been below ₦5,280,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the reward for land in the context of production?
questions.explanation: The reward for land as a factor of production is rent. Land is a natural resource that is used in the production process, and owners of land receive payment in the form of rent for its use. This distinguishes it from other factors of production, such as labor and capital, which have different rewards.

distractorRationale.a: Wages are the reward for labor, not land.
distractorRationale.c: Profit is the reward for entrepreneurship, not land.
distractorRationale.d: Interest is the reward for capital, not land.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of labor as a factor of production?
questions.explanation: Labor is not indestructible; it can be affected by various factors such as health and age. Unlike land and capital, which can be maintained and preserved, labor is subject to deterioration over time and can be lost.

distractorRationale.a: Labor is indeed mobile, allowing workers to move to different jobs.
distractorRationale.b: Labor is heterogeneous, meaning that workers have different skills and abilities.
distractorRationale.d: Labor can be trained to improve skills and productivity.

questions.stem: What is the primary reward for capital in the production process?
questions.explanation: The primary reward for capital in the production process is interest. Capital refers to the financial resources used to fund production, and those who provide capital typically receive interest as compensation for its use.

distractorRationale.a: Wages are the reward for labor, not capital.
distractorRationale.b: Profit is the reward for entrepreneurship, not capital.
distractorRationale.c: Rent is the reward for land, not capital.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the concept of specialization?

options.text: Workers focus on a single task to increase efficiency.
It involves using multiple resources at once.
It reduces the need for labor.

questions.explanation: Specialization occurs when workers focus on a single task, which enhances efficiency and productivity. By concentrating on specific tasks, workers can develop expertise and improve their performance, leading to increased output.

distractorRationale.b: Specialization does not involve using multiple resources at once; it focuses on one task.
distractorRationale.c: Specialization can increase the need for labor in certain areas due to increased production.
distractorRationale.d: Diversifying production activities is the opposite of specialization.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a limitation of division of labor?
questions.explanation: A significant limitation of division of labor is that it can lead to boredom among workers. When individuals perform the same repetitive tasks, they may become disengaged, which can reduce overall job satisfaction and productivity.

distractorRationale.a: Increased productivity is a benefit, not a limitation.
distractorRationale.c: Division of labor often reduces opportunities for skill development.
distractorRationale.d: Higher quality output is typically a benefit of division of labor.

questions.stem: Which factor of production is considered the 'organizer' of the other factors?

distractorRationale.a: Land is a natural resource, not an organizer.
distractorRationale.b: Labor refers to human effort, not organization.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the characteristics of capital as a factor of production?

options.text: It is durable and can be reused.

questions.explanation: Capital is characterized as durable and can be reused in the production process. Unlike labor, which is perishable, capital goods such as machinery and equipment can last for a long time and be utilized repeatedly in production.

distractorRationale.a: Capital is not naturally occurring; it is created through investment.
distractorRationale.c: Capital is not perishable; it can be maintained over time.
distractorRationale.d: Capital can indeed be accumulated through savings and investment.

questions.stem: What is one of the main advantages of specialization in production?

It eliminates the need for training.

questions.explanation: One of the main advantages of specialization is that it increases the overall output. By allowing workers to focus on specific tasks, they become more efficient and productive, leading to higher levels of production.

distractorRationale.c: Training is still necessary, even with specialization.

distractorRationale.a: Land provides resources but does not create goods directly.
distractorRationale.c: Capital supports production but does not create goods without labor.
